question: Should OpenClaw accept `includeFamily` as the supported opt-in Gateway and `sessions_history` contract for reading reset-family transcript ancestors, while rejecting `includeFamily` with `offset`?
rationale: The code path is no longer blocked on a narrow mechanical defect; the remaining question is whether this new model-facing/protocol-visible archived-history surface is the product and security boundary maintainers want.

options.title: Accept `includeFamily`
options.body: Merge once exact-head checks are green and a maintainer confirms the opt-in reset-family history semantics and offset rejection are the permanent API.

options.title: Revise the history API
options.body: Ask for a different selector name, response shape, or offset behavior if maintainers want a broader archive-history contract before exposing this surface.

options.title: Defer to a broader design
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want one canonical design covering archive recovery, UI browsing, session family lookup, and compaction history together.

recommendation.title: Accept `includeFamily`
recommendation.body: Merge once exact-head checks are green and a maintainer confirms the opt-in reset-family history semantics and offset rejection are the permanent API.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent `sessions_history` pagination work makes this person the clearest owner for the new selector and offset interaction.
